discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 151115
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
615 AM EST Sun Nov 15 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Some low clouds linger today with continued slightly below 
  normal high temperatures from 45 to 50.

- A moderating temperature trend expecting this week with a
  return of above normal temperatures. The warmest days appear 
  to be Thursday through Saturday with many locations 
  experiencing highs in the low to mid 60s.

- Mainly dry conditions are expected this week with some rain
  chances returning by next weekend.


&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 230 AM EST Sun Nov 15 2026

Another upper level vort max continues to drop south across the 
Great Lakes region early this morning. Moisture profiles have become 
quite shallow over the past 24 hours with successive periods of mid 
level dry air advection in the active short wave pattern. Mainly dry 
conditions are expected today, although cannot rule out some patchy 
light drizzle accompanying passage of this vort max through daybreak 
given the shallow moisture profiles in place and weak lingering low 
level lift. Continued northerly low level flow today and maintenance 
of thin layer of higher RH beneath weak 5k ft based inversion will 
likely keep good deal of low clouds around although pockets of 
stronger mid level subsidence will allow for some sun in spots.
An expansive 1030mb anticyclone will continue to build in from 
the Mid MS River Valley today which will weaken the low level 
flow this afternoon resulting in poor mixing. Poor mixing 
combined with more of a neutral thermal advection pattern will 
result in similar high temperatures today as observed yesterday 
(perhaps just a little warmer).

Backing and weakening of the low level flow tonight should 
result in better opportunity for scattering low clouds, although
would not be surprised if spots, especially east of I-69 into 
NW Ohio maintain some low cloud cover as guidance continues to 
hint at another weak mid/upper level perturbation backdooring 
across the eastern Great Lakes. Min temperatures are of lower 
confidence tonight given this cloud cover dependency and just 
hedged slightly cooler than model blended guidance. 

Monday should finally feature more aggressive positive mid 
level height tendencies as Upper Midwest mid level ridge shifts 
eastward. An associated weak low level westerly flow regime will
set up, but thermal gradients in this pattern are quite weak 
with only modest low level warm advection developing. However, 
Monday will start a moderating trend that will continue into 
the weekend.

Guidance has been fairly consistent in a progressive eastern Pacific 
wave pattern, with the first of these more pronounced waves in 
the late Wednesday to Thursday timeframe. Moisture return of any
significance looks hard to come by at this time due to stubborn
SE CONUS low/mid level ridging with better moisture transport 
downstream of this short wave likely getting pinched off across 
the southern and central Plains. Some elevated moisture return 
is likely into the Great Lakes region late Wednesday into 
Thursday but with bulk of forcing staying north of local area 
this would probably be just a very light rain/sprinkle event if 
anything, and confined to NW IN/SW Lower MI. This short wave 
will not have a deep latitudinal connection and mid/upper 
ridging should aggressively build back in for Friday in advance 
a more robust upper level short wave depicted in medium range 
guidance. This should result in Friday/Saturday being the 
warmest days of the period as broad warm sector develops from 
Ohio Valley to the southern Great Lakes. Highs these days should
reach low-mid 60s and possibly into upper 60s Saturday 
depending on timing of increasing cloud cover.

While medium range guidance is in good agreement with this wave 
across western CONUS, a good deal of uncertainty arises for next 
weekend regarding potential phasing with southern Canadian branch of 
westerlies. This will impact how far south better dynamics can reach 
and the magnitude of northward extent of better low level moisture 
transport. Given at least large scale signal consensus in 
medium range guidance, low to mid range chance shower PoPs have 
been maintained for next weekend with potentially a cool down 
back to near seasonable levels (briefly?) for early next week.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z MONDAY/...
Issued at 611 AM EST Sun Nov 15 2026

VFR conditions at the terminals for the most part, outside of
MVFR ceilings this morning at KSBN. KFWA sat on the very edge of
a BKN015-BKN025 cloud deck all night, which is shifting further
eastward as of this writing (KSMD has been around 1500 ft all
night). Model guidance now appears to keep this cloud deck east
through the day, so shifted to a more optimistic forecast. It's
possible KSBN could maintain BKN025-BKN030 for longer than 
current forecast, but most of guidance improves ceilings to 
3500-5000ft by late morning/early afternoon. 

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Marsili

spc.text:
SPC AC 151607

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1007 AM CST Sun Nov 15 2026

   Valid 151630Z - 161200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON
   AND EVENING ALONG THE MIDDLE TEXAS GULF COAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A strong thunderstorm or two may affect the middle Texas coast this
   afternoon and evening.

   ...Middle Texas Gulf Coast...
   Overall, the risk of severe storms appears to have diminished for
   later today.  Scattered intense thunderstorms have been occurring
   offshore over the warm shelf waters, but that activity is not
   expected to build westward and inland.  Other showers and
   thunderstorms associated with an approaching cold front over central
   TX will move into the CRP/HOU areas later today, but the air mass is
   only marginally unstable with dewpoints only in the 50s.  A strong
   storm or two capable of gusty winds may occur around/after sunset as
   the front approaches the coast, but the overall threat appears
   rather low.

   ..Hart/Halbert-E.. 11/15/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 151642

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1042 AM CST Sun Nov 15 2026

   Valid 161200Z - 171200Z

   ...NO THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorm potential appears low on Monday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A mid/upper-level shortwave trough is forecast to amplify on Monday
   as it approaches the CA coast. Downstream of this trough, an upper
   ridge will continue to build across the central CONUS, while a
   positive-tilt upper trough remains in place over the East.

   A modest increase in moisture is possible late in the period across
   southern CA/NV and western AZ, in advance of the approaching
   shortwave trough. Very isolated/sporadic lightning flashes cannot be
   ruled out with this system, but thunderstorm potential generally
   appears low due to very weak buoyancy. Otherwise, an expansive
   surface ridge over the central/eastern CONUS will limit
   moisture/instability and thunderstorm potential elsewhere through
   the period.

   ..Dean.. 11/15/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 150828

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0228 AM CST Sun Nov 15 2026

   Valid 171200Z - 181200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are unlikely Tuesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   The upper trough over the West Coast is forecast to move eastward
   across the Southwest and into the Rockies Tuesday. An associated
   surface low will deepen over the central/northern High Plains
   supporting increasing southerly flow over the Southwest. While still
   quite limited, some increase in surface moisture is expected ahead
   of the trough and cold front. The increasing ascent and cooler
   mid-level temperatures should be sufficient for weak destabilization
   and isolated thunderstorms Tuesday afternoon into early Wednesday
   across the Four Corners and Western Slope. Given the expected very
   weak buoyancy, severe storms are not anticipated.

   Late Tuesday into early Wednesday a second upper low and associated
   cold front will approach the West Coast. Weak buoyancy is again
   forecast across northern CA and OR, which may be sufficient to
   support occasional lightning.

   To the east, strong high pressure will remain entrenched across the
   Midwest with offshore flow and dry/stable conditions dominating much
   of the US. The exception will be across the southern and eastern
   peninsula of Florida. Here, onshore flow may allow for modest
   destabilization with a few thunderstorms possible along the sea
   breeze through the afternoon. Severe storms are unlikely.

   ..Lyons.. 11/15/2026
